# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only a large, smooth button; the display, light, and all three wire properties are still unknown to me. I am asking Mute to read the manual, establish a simple visual yes/no code with Deaf, and relay Deaf’s observations and the required action to me through speech. No bomb action is safe yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large smooth button. I cannot identify the display, light, or wires yet. Please read the manual and establish a simple gesture code with Deaf for reporting those visual facts, then tell me the exact safe operation and any required wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, a green light, one large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Wait for Mute's manual-based instructions.

I now know the bomb’s visible facts from Deaf: display 0, green light, a large “PUSH TO DEFUSE” button, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. The manual instructions are still missing, so I must not press or cut anything. I will relay the complete observations to Mute and request the exact safe action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light green; button says PUSH TO DEFUSE; wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Please consult the manual and tell me exactly whether to push or cut, and which wire position if cutting.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled me four gestures: thumbs up, pointing up, thumbs down, open hand. No gesture code has been established, so do not treat them as instructions. The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.

Mute’s gestures cannot be interpreted because no code was established, and Deaf’s facts remain the only reliable bomb observations. Since Mute is the manual reader and can speak to me, I need the manual’s literal instruction rather than another gesture sequence. I will request the exact operation and prohibit guessing.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are unusable without a prearranged code. Please speak the manual's exact instruction to me: PUSH or CUT, and the wire position if applicable. Do not gesture the instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute's gestures are not an agreed code; wait for Mute's spoken manual instructions.

The manual instruction still has not reached me as speech. Deaf’s visual report is unchanged, but it does not determine whether pressing or cutting is safe. I will not perform an irreversible action based on the unrecognized gestures; I will again request the literal manual instruction from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received your manual instruction in speech. State exactly: PUSH, or CUT position 1, 2, or 3. I will not act on gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute cannot speak. I have established an action code and am waiting for the manual's decoded instruction. Do not act yet.

Mute cannot provide the manual instruction by speech, and the gestures have not been decoded for me. Deaf has established an action code and is awaiting the manual’s decoded result, so no physical action is justified yet. I will wait for Deaf to communicate the decoded operation in a form I can receive.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The manual instruction received from Mute is: cut wire 1, the red wire. Do not press the button or cut another wire.

Deaf reports that Mute’s manual instruction is to cut wire 1, the red wire. This is specific and consistent with the observed wire layout, so I will perform exactly that action and nothing else.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
